mystăgōgus , i, m., = μυσταγωγός,
I.one who conducts a person through secret and sacred places as a guide, an initiator, a mystagogue, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 59, § 132.— Trop.: “amicitiae meae, te mystagogo usus, accessit,” the founder, Symm. Ep. 5, 64 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
